title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Islamabad. Tip #1
body: Old money says "we're in F-6/3." New money says "we're in Phase 8, Overseas Block." One gives you a sector and a street. The other gives you a society, a phase, and a block. That single sentence is the whole class system and neither of them notices they're doing it. It's a sealed deal when you realise one house has a number and the other has a name on a plaque.

title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Islamabad. Tip #2
body: Old money lives in a 1979 kothi in F-6 with original marble, a mulberry tree, and a kitchen nobody has touched since 1994. New money lives in Bahria with Roman pillars, a lift, and a chandelier visible from the road. Old money will not renovate. New money renovated last year and knows the per-square-foot. It's a sealed deal if the older lawn is too big to maintain and nobody is maintaining it.

title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Islamabad. Tip #3
body: Old money drives a white Prado with a dent. New money drives an Audi e-tron, two years old, washed weekly. Both cost about the same. Only one is trying. It's a sealed deal if the Prado's driver has been with that family longer than the newer family has had money.

title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Islamabad. Tip #4
body: Listen to how the school gets said. Old money says "Froebel's" or nothing at all, and moves on, because everyone already worked it out. New money names the school and then mentions the fees. Identical information. Completely different transaction. It's a sealed deal if someone adds "my father went there too" and finds it unremarkable.

title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Islamabad. Tip #5
body: Old money is at the Islamabad Club because their father was, and the waiting list is a story other people tell. New money applied in 2017, knows someone on the committee, and is still waiting. This is the one thing money cannot speed up and it drives people genuinely mad. It's a sealed deal if a family walks in and signs nothing.

title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Islamabad. Tip #6
body: Old money does the wedding at Serena or a farmhouse in Chak Shahzad with six hundred people. New money books the Convention Centre and the singer's fee circulates for a week afterwards. The spend is comparable. Only one wants the number in the air. It's a sealed deal if a lawn has hosted three generations of the same family's weddings.

title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Islamabad. Tip #7
body: Ask what the family does. Old money says "my father was in the service" and stops, and that sentence is doing an enormous amount of work. New money describes construction, property, and a franchise, and one of them is earning. It's a sealed deal if the answer is about a posting rather than a business.

title: How to (Accidentally) Tell Old Money from New Money in Islamabad. Tip #8
body: Here's what nobody admits: new money is having a better time. Better parties, better cars, actual enthusiasm about being alive. Old money is in a house that needs rewiring, being quietly certain, faintly bored. Everyone claims to respect the second and everyone wants the invitation from the first. It's a sealed deal when a family has been comfortable long enough to find it dull.
